newsitem.title: FRANCE: Goldman Sachs analyst upgrades Danone.
newsitem.headline: Goldman Sachs analyst upgrades Danone.

text.p: Goldman Sachs has upgraded its recommendation on French food group Danone, the London-based analyst for the U.S. brokerage said on Thursday.
The analyst told Reuters he has upgraded Danone to "trading buy" from "market performer", and not to "market outperformer" as rumoured in the market.

The upgrade was based on the weakness in Danone shares in recent months and the group's maintained forecast of a six percent increase in 1996 net attributable profit. However, there was still some caution on the stock, which was reflected in the recommendation as a short-term buy, he said.

Among the concerns are Danone's continued over-dependence on the European market, which is "structurally difficult," and its lack of presence in emerging markets. Moves to develop that presence would require time and large amounts of money.
Danone was up 30 francs at 722, or 4.34 percent, at 1342 GMT.
Societe Generale Delahaye has upgraded the stock to "outperform" from "neutral" in view of its market performance.
Danone shares hit 812 francs per share on July 4 and a year-high of 830 on March 27.
